<h>Lectio 1</h>
De libro Apocalýpsis beáti Joánnis Apóstoli
<r>Apo 2:1-4</r>
<n>1</n> Angelo Ephesi ecclésiæ scribe: Hæc dicit, qui tenet septem stellas in déxtera sua, qui ámbulat in médio septem candelabrórum aureórum:
<n>2</n> Scio ópera tua, et labórem, et patiéntiam tuam, et quia non potes sustinére malos: et tentásti eos, qui se dicunt apóstolos esse, et non sunt: et invenísti eos mendáces:
<n>3</n> Et patiéntiam habes, et sustinuísti propter nomen meum, et non defecísti.
<n>4</n> Sed hábeo advérsum te, quod caritátem tuam primam reliquísti.
<r>℣.</r> Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nostri.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<r>℟.</r> Locútus est ad me unus ex septem Angelis, dicens: Veni, osténdam tibi novam nuptam, sponsam Agni:
* Et vidi Jerúsalem descendéntem de cælo, ornátam monílibus suis, allelúia, allelúia, allelúia.
<r>℣.</r> Et sústulit me in spíritu in montem magnum et altum.
<r>℟.</r> Et vidi Jerúsalem descendéntem de cælo, ornátam monílibus suis, allelúia, allelúia, allelúia.

<h>Reading 1</h>
Lesson from the book of Revelation
<r>Rev 2:1-4</r>
<n>1</n> Unto the angel of the church of Ephesus write: These things saith he, who holdeth the seven stars in his right hand, who walketh in the midst of the seven golden candlesticks:
<n>2</n> I know thy works, and thy labour, and thy patience, and how thou canst not bear them that are evil, and thou hast tried them, who say they are apostles, and are not, and hast found them liars:
<n>3</n> And thou hast patience, and hast endured for my name, and hast not fainted.
<n>4</n> But I have somewhat against thee, because thou hast left thy first charity.
<r>℣.</r> But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<r>℟.</r> One of the seven Angels talked with me, saying: Come hither, I will show thee the bride, the Lamb's wife.
* And I saw Jerusalem descending out of heaven, adorned with her jewels. Alleluia, Alleluia, Alleluia.
<r>℣.</r> And he carried me away in the Spirit to a great and high mountain
<r>℟.</r> And I saw Jerusalem descending out of heaven, adorned with her jewels. Alleluia, Alleluia, Alleluia.

<r>℣.</r> Dómine, exáudi oratiónem meam.
<r>℟.</r> Et clamor meus ad te véniat.
<c>O</c>rémus.
<c>P</c>ræsta, quǽsumus, omnípotens Deus: ut qui paschália festa perégimus, hæc, te largiénte, móribus et vita teneámus.
<h>P</h>er Dóminum nostrum Jesum Christum, Fílium tuum: qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitáte Spíritus Sancti, Deus, per ómnia sǽcula sæculórum.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
b.e5577cb863:
<h>Prayer</h>
<r>℣.</r> O Lord, hear my prayer.
<r>℟.</r> And let my cry come unto thee.
<c>L</c>et us pray.
<c>G</c>rant, we beseech Thee, almighty God, that we who have celebrated the Paschal Feast, may, by Thy bounty, retain its fruits in our daily habits and behaviour.
<h>T</h>hrough Jesus Christ, thy Son our Lord, Who liveth and reigneth with thee, in the unity of the Holy Ghost, God, world without end.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.

b.becd9938ce:
<h>Martyrologium</h>
<c>S</c>éptimo Idus Aprílis Luna prima. Anno Dómini 2027
<h>R</h>otómagi natális sancti Joánnis Baptístæ de La Salle, Presbýteri et Confessóris, qui, in erudiénda adolescéntia præsértim páupere excéllens, et de religióne civilíque societáte præcláre méritus, Fratrum Scholárum Christianárum Sodalitátem instítuit. Eum Pius Duodécimus, Póntifex Máximus, ómnium Magistrórum púeris adolescentibúsque instituéndis præcípuum apud Deum cæléstem Patrónum constítuit. Ipsíus tamen festum Idibus Maii celebrátur.
<h>I</h>n Africa item natális sanctórum Mártyrum Epiphánii Epíscopi, Donáti, Rufíni et aliórum trédecim.
<h>A</h>lexandríæ sancti Peléusii, Presbýteri et Mártyris.
<h>S</h>ynópe, in Ponto, sanctórum ducentórum Mártyrum.
<h>I</h>n Cilícia sancti Calliópii Mártyris, qui, sub Maximiáno Præfécto, post ália torménta, cápite in terram verso cruci affíxus, nóbili coróna martýrii decorátus est.
<h>N</h>icomedíæ sancti Cyríaci et aliórum decem Mártyrum.
<h>V</h>erónæ sancti Saturníni, Epíscopi et Confessóris.
<h>R</h>omæ sancti Hegesíppi, qui, vicínus Apostolórum tempóribus, Romam venit ad Anicétum Pontíficem, ibíque mansit usque ad Eleuthérium, et Ecclesiasticórum Actuum a passióne Dómini usque ad suam ætátem sermóne símplici texuit históriam; ut, quorum vitam sectabátur, dicéndi quoque exprímeret charactére.
<h>I</h>n Sýria sancti Aphraátis Anachorétæ, qui, Valéntis témpore, cathólicam fidem virtúte miraculórum advérsus Ariános deféndit.
<r>℣.</r> Et álibi aliórum plurimórum sanctórum Mártyrum et Confessórum, atque sanctárum Vírginum.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.
b.67f2d00f4e:
<h>Martyrology</h>
<c>A</c>pril 7th 2027, the 1st day of the Moon, were born into the better life:
<h>A</h>t Rouen, [in the year 17 19,] the holy Confessor John Baptist de la Salle. He was foremost in the teaching of the young, the poor especially, and deserved well of both religion and civil society. He founded the Congregation of the Brothers of the Christian Schools.
<h>I</h>n Africa, the holy martyrs Epiphanius, the Bishop, also Donatus, Rufinus, and thirteen others.
<h>A</h>t Alexandria, the holy martyr Peleusius the Priest.
<h>A</h>t Synope, in Pontus, two hundred holy martyrs, [in the year 310.]
<h>[</h>At Soti,] in Cilicia, the holy martyr Calliopius, who after diverse torments under the prefect Maximian was crucified head downwards, and so gained a noble crown of martyrdom, [in the year 304.]
<h>A</h>t Nicomedia, the holy martyrs Cyriacus and ten others.
<h>A</h>t Verona, the holy Confessor Saturninus, Bishop of that see, [in the fourth century.]
<h>A</h>t Rome, holy Hegesippus, who came to Pope Anicetus, at Rome, [in the year 157,] very soon after the time of the Apostles, and abode there until the time of Pope Eleutherius, [and died in the year 180.] He wrote in plain words a Church history from the Passion of the Lord until his own time, to set forth the lives of those in whose footsteps he followed.
<h>I</h>n Syria, the holy Hermit Aphraates, who defended the Catholic faith by the power of his miracles against the Arians, in the time of the Emperor Valens.
<r>℣.</r> And elsewhere many other holy martyrs, confessors, and holy virgins.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

b.ebdc957211:
<h>Oratio</h>
<r>℣.</r> Dóminus vobíscum.
<r>℟.</r> Et cum spíritu tuo.
<c>O</c>rémus.
<c>P</c>ræsta, quǽsumus, omnípotens Deus: ut qui paschália festa perégimus, hæc, te largiénte, móribus et vita teneámus.
<h>P</h>er Dóminum nostrum Jesum Christum, Fílium tuum: qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitáte Spíritus Sancti, Deus, per ómnia sǽcula sæculórum.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
b.d23df9fc67:
<h>Prayer</h>
<r>℣.</r> The Lord be with you.
<r>℟.</r> And with thy spirit.
<c>L</c>et us pray.
<c>G</c>rant, we beseech Thee, almighty God, that we who have celebrated the Paschal Feast, may, by Thy bounty, retain its fruits in our daily habits and behaviour.
<h>T</h>hrough Jesus Christ, thy Son our Lord, Who liveth and reigneth with thee, in the unity of the Holy Ghost, God, world without end.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
